# Glossary review: Hindi (`hi`)

*Written by `python scripts/intake/glossary_tool.py record`; `check` compares it with a fresh run. Do not edit it.*

Glossary version `1.0.0-draft`. These are DRAFTS until you approve them.

## What to check

1. Is the canonical form the word a trader of this language really uses for the term?
2. Are the other accepted spellings words a trader would also type (a short form, a plural, a verb form)? A question that contains any of them is recognised as containing the term.
3. Does any spelling also mean something else in this language? It would mark an unrelated question.
4. Do the texts below read naturally, say what the English says, and keep each `{name}` placeholder?

| intake.reason.mcd0_defect_m15 | The M15 channel does not fit the price well enough, so readings that use it are cautionary. | M15 चैनल कीमत से पर्याप्त मेल नहीं खाता, इसलिए इसे इस्तेमाल करने वाली रीडिंग सावधानी माँगती हैं। |

| intake.reason.modifier_caution | Another sensor adds caution to this reading: {state}. | एक और सेंसर इस रीडिंग में सावधानी जोड़ता है: {state}। |

## Sign-off

Read the tables above, then edit `approval.json` in this folder: set `status` to `APPROVED`, `approved_by` to your name and `approved_on` to the date (YYYY-MM-DD). It holds the SHA-256 of the content you read, so a later change to it puts this area back to PENDING (`python scripts/intake/glossary_tool.py record`). Then run `record` once more so the forms of Hindi are marked `approved` in the glossary.
